findings.heading: Pull and push changes up to Github
findings.proposition: English concludes the note with 'it is better to PUSH when you are done with introducing changes on the task you were working on'; the Turkish concludes 'commit etmek daha iyidir' (it is better to COMMIT).
findings.reader_consequence: The note's whole premise is that committed-but-unpushed changes are easy to revert while pushed ones are not, so the advice must be about timing the PUSH. A Turkish reader gets advice to delay committing instead, which contradicts the chapter's repeated instruction to commit often and small, and leaves them unsure when to push.

findings.heading: Pull and push changes up to Github > In Rstudio
findings.proposition: English states that the RStudio 'Pull' icon (downward arrow) fetches and pulls at the same time; the Turkish says only to click the icon and drops 'which fetches and pulls at the same time'.
findings.reader_consequence: The chapter elsewhere teaches fetch and pull as two distinct operations. A Turkish reader is not told that the one RStudio button performs both, so they may look for a separate fetch control in RStudio or believe they must fetch some other way before pulling.

findings.heading: Pull and push changes up to Github > In Rstudio
findings.proposition: English says the linked tutorial chapters show how to connect to a repository using an SSH key, and warns it is 'more complicated'; the Turkish keeps only 'see chapters 10 and 11 of this tutorial to connect to a repository'.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader tired of typing a password is not told what the remedy actually is (an SSH key) nor that it is harder than the methods already shown, so they cannot judge whether to follow the link.

findings.heading: Vocabulary, concepts and basic functions > Commits
findings.proposition: English gives the reason for splitting the model-script and figure-script work into two commits: 'it would be easier in case you wanted to revert the changes on the figure but not the model'. The Turkish parenthesis is truncated to 'sekildeki degisiklikleri geri almak isteyip modeli' and never states the 'but not the model' contrast or the ease-of-reverting rationale.
findings.reader_consequence: The example loses its point. A Turkish reader sees an instruction to make two commits with no reason, so they cannot generalise the rule (group changes so that any one group can be reverted alone) to their own work.

findings.heading: What is Git?
findings.proposition: English says Git works like the 'track change' option in Word, LibreOffice or Google docs 'but for all types of files'; the Turkish keeps the analogy and drops 'but for all types of files'.
findings.reader_consequence: The clause is the point of the analogy: it tells the reader Git is not limited to text documents and tracks scripts, data files and images too. Without it a Turkish reader may assume Git only versions word-processor-like documents.

findings.heading: Resources
findings.proposition: English lists the resource URL https://tutorialzine.com/2016/06/learn-git-in-30-minutes; the Turkish gives https://tutorialzine.com/2016/06/learn-git-in-30-dakika, with the word 'minutes' inside the URL path translated to 'dakika'.
findings.reader_consequence: The link is dead. A Turkish reader who clicks the recommended 'basic and advanced' tutorial gets a 404 and has no way to guess the correct address.

findings.heading: Resources
findings.proposition: English lists https://ohi-science.org/news/github-going-back-in-time; the Turkish lists https://ohi-science.org/news/github-coming-back-in-time ('going' changed to 'coming').
findings.reader_consequence: The link is dead, so a Turkish reader loses the recommended article on reverting a Git repository to an earlier state.

findings.heading: Setup > Install an interface (optional but recommended)
findings.proposition: English states that the RStudio Git pane and Github Desktop are the two beginner interfaces 'which we will showcase in this chapter'; the Turkish renders this as 'ki bu bolumde durum nasil olacak', which does not state that the chapter demonstrates those two interfaces.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader is not told that the two named beginner tools are the ones the rest of the chapter walks through, so they may install one of the intermediate clients named in the next sentence and then find no matching instructions.
